newsitem.title: USA: Kitty Hawk doubles fleet since going public.
newsitem.headline: Kitty Hawk doubles fleet since going public.

text.p: Freighter operator Kitty Hawk said it has virtually doubled its fleet in the space of six months since going public last October.

"We have added seven 727-200s to the eight we had in service at our IPO (Initial Public Offering)," chairman Tom Christopher said Tuesday accompanying Q1 total revenues for the quarter rising 39 percent to $28.1 million.
"Four of the new planes are already in service, with the remaining three planned for service prior to the beginning of the third quarter" of 1997.
Christopher added that Kitty Hawk's business margins in the airfreight sector were not materially impacted by recent high fuel prices since customers pay the fuel bills.
Carriers like Kitty Hawk or Denver-based Atlas Air typically provide customers with airline, crew, maintenance and insurance (ACMI), with customers paying for fuel and groundhandling.

Besides operating ACMI freighters for contract customers, Kitty Hawk provides on-demand cargo charters throughout the Americas, Europe and the Pacific, mainly as a facilitator using aircraft chartered from other airlines. However, Christopher said the company would like to expand its fleet to bring as much as half of that cargo chartering in house.

"Based on current strong demand for the company's services, and the continued addition of cargo airplanes, management anticipates further positive momentum through the remainder of the year," the company said.
The company booked 2,881 on-demand charters compared with 2,333 a year earlier 1996.

Kitty Hawk's ACMI operations for other airlines achieved a 36 percent increase in flight hours: 5,830 compared with 4,292 a year ago, helping boost revenues for this segment of its business by 48 percent to $14.9 million. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
